description: Semantic vocabulary for solution-oriented Build Ideas. Cohesion is intentionally absent: recommendation compatibility is always optimized.

relations.description: Directly satisfies the named mechanic or Fate obligation.
Causes the named ailment or control state.
Creates a mechanic, resource, defensive layer, or recovery loop.
Improves or changes a mechanic without proving that the entity creates it.
Needs the named mechanic, state, resource, equipment, or access condition.
Spends or removes the named setup state or resource.
Produces the named setup state or resource.
Transforms one named mechanic or damage type into another.
Makes one mechanic operate as another instead.
Explicitly disables, forbids, or removes access to the named mechanic.
Restricts access to a named ascendancy or other exclusive source.
Consumes an equipment or other mutually exclusive slot.
Creates a proxy, minion, totem, object, or persistent setup element.
Authoritatively classifies the entity without asserting that it fulfills an obligation.

confidence_levels.description: Direct structured source field or unambiguous explicit clause.
Deterministic interpretation with a clear native mechanical relationship.
Useful interpretation that must not alone establish a hard compatibility claim.

candidate_roles.description: Candidate for the package's principal damage delivery.
Applies a state, debuff, or control effect used by another piece.
Consumes or rewards a setup state.
Makes another package element legal, reliable, or materially stronger.
Adds avoidance, mitigation, a buffer, or resilience.
Restores Life, Energy Shield, Mana, or another sustaining resource.
Adds mobility, reservation, convenience, or situational support.

offense_semantics.description: Poison has a native Chaos relationship; generic Chaos damage does not establish Poison fulfillment.

package_obligations.survivability: Find a credible complementary defensive layer and a credible recovery loop unless the selected package already supplies them.
package_obligations.unresolved_policy: Report an unresolved requirement instead of filling a content-type quota with a weak recommendation.
